text.p: Tyler Corp said Thursday it expects a 1996 loss of $2.90 to $3.00 a share but is confident it will return to profitability in 1997.

Tyler said the 1996 loss will include a charge of $2.83 to $2.87 a share for the write-off of $52 million of goodwill and other intangibles at Forest City Auto Parts and Institutional Financing Services, and $7 to $8 million of pre-tax restructuring and other charges.
Operating profit before restructuring and other charges for calendar 1996 is expected to be $3.2 to $3.8 million, compared to $4 million in 1995, it said.

The restructuring and other charges are for excess inventory at IFS and Forest City, store closings at Forest City, lease commitments on vacant corporate facilities, severance pay and other obligations relating to termination of employees, and settlement of certain employee-benefit plans that were discontinued in 1996.
Tyler provides products for fund-raising programs and retails automotive parts.
